questions.stem: A 58-year-old man presents with progressive lower extremity edema and nephrotic-range proteinuria (6.5 g/24h). Serum creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL. A renal biopsy reveals mesangial expansion with Congo red-negative fibrillar deposits on electron microscopy measuring 18 nm in diameter, arranged randomly. Immunohistochemistry is strongly positive for DNAJB9. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.sourceExplanation: Fibrillary glomerulonephritis (FGN) 的典型電子顯微鏡特徵為 16-24 nm (平均約 18-20 nm) 無分支、隨機排列之 Solid Fibrils，且 Congo Red Staining 通常為 Negative。DNAJB9 (Heat Shock Protein Co-chaperone) 為 FGN 的 Highly Sensitive & Specific Biomarker (Sensitivity > 98%)。Amyloidosis 的 Fibril 8-12 nm 且 Congo Red Positive；Immunotactoid Glomerulopathy 的 Microtubules 30-50 nm 且具 Hollow Center 與 Parallel Stacks 結構。

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) develops nephrotic syndrome. Renal biopsy displays lobular mesangial expansion. What is the most appropriate next step in clinical management?

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man presents with fatigue, weight loss, macroglossia, and nephrotic syndrome. Renal biopsy shows mesangial expansion with weakly PAS-positive material.
